internal.title: Incident Report: High Latency in Ad Service Due to Flag Activation
internal.body:
At 11:40 UTC on 2026-11-08, a high latency alert was triggered for the ad service. Investigation identified that enabling the adHighCpu flag caused significant performance degradation, increasing latency and error rates. The flag was disabled at 12:00 UTC, resulting in recovery to normal latency levels as verified by monitoring metrics. The incident was resolved promptly with no lasting impact on service availability.

Timeline:
- 11:40:58 Alert received for high latency in ad service
- 12:00:39 Diagnosis confirmed latency linked to adHighCpu flag
- 12:00:40 Flag disable action proposed and approved
- 12:00:41 Flag disabled
- 12:00:41 Recovery verified by latency metrics

Root Cause:
The root cause was the activation of the adHighCpu flag, which introduced performance degradation in the ad service.

Resolution:
Disabling the adHighCpu flag restored normal service latency.

Lessons Learned:
- Feature flags impacting CPU usage should be carefully tested under load before enabling in production.
- Monitoring flag states alongside latency metrics can accelerate diagnosis.

Action Items:
- Review testing protocols for CPU-intensive feature flags.
- Enhance alerting to correlate flag changes with latency spikes.

external.body: Between 11:40 and 12:00 UTC on 2026-11-08, the ad service experienced elevated latency affecting performance. The issue was identified and resolved by disabling a recently enabled configuration change. Normal service performance has been restored. We apologize for any inconvenience caused and appreciate your understanding.
